name: Chip supply
summary: China's rare-earth export pause lapses 10 Nov unless Beijing publishes a notice; no TSMC or Samsung stoppage found
state: China's suspension of its expanded rare-earth export controls ends on 10 Nov, and no formal notice extending it had been published by 5 Nov (Motley Fool). The US and China announced an extension of their wider trade truce to 10 Jan 2027 in late September, which US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent says covers the rare-earth controls. Earlier licensing controls on seven medium and heavy rare earths remain in place (Startup Fortune). Searches on 8 Nov found no TSMC or Samsung output stoppage.
for_you: Electronics, car and defence manufacturers that depend on Chinese rare-earth magnets and materials are most exposed if the expanded controls return.
rubric_hit: Watch: export controls at issue, with the rare-earth pause due to lapse 10 Nov. Alert line not met: no major disruption to TSMC or Samsung output found.

sources.title: The Motley Fool — China's Rare-Earth Export Pause Expires Nov. 10
Startup Fortune — China's Rare Earth Export Truce Expires November 10 With No Renewal in Sight

why: Advanced chips underpin everything from phones to AI to weapons; supply is concentrated in Taiwan and Korea.
drivers: Export controls, Taiwan risk, fab outages, AI demand, materials.

rubric.alert: Major disruption to TSMC/Samsung output, or controls halting a major supply chain.
rubric.watch: New export controls, shortages reported in key segments, or a fab outage.
rubric.normal: Supply normal; no new major controls.
